newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Life assurance giant Sanlam is to scale down its 20 billion rand industrial portfolio and consider listing, chairman Marinus Daling told the Financial Times of London.

- The death toll from clashes on property in and around two Randgold mines in Northwest province rose to 21 on Tuesday, with 38 people injured, and tension remains high as police patrol affected areas.
- South Africa has begun talks on a possible World Bank loan to help finance improvements in its international competitiveness.

- The government has been forced to add to its debt mountain to escape the short-term pressure of a more massive interest bill than it already has, with the finance department forced to sell paper at a much larger discount than anticipated.
- Senior ANC and IFP negotiators will hold talks on Wednesday to discuss Inkatha's possible return to the Constitutional Assembly.
- Minister of water affairs Kader Asmal has sacked South Africa's senior delegate to the troubled $4 billion Lesotho Highlands Water project.
- C.G. Smith has bought a further 20 percent of Island View Holdings from Afcol, raising its stake to 80 percent.

- About 2,000 people gathered at the Braamfontein cemetry in Johannesburg on Tuesday to witness President Nelson Mandela pronounce the grave of Enoch Mankayi Sontonga, composer of the the national anthem Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika, a national monument.
